Dimensions 10,11,12 have explicit small-orbit negative witnesses, with smaller radius exclusions by exact two-shell eigenvalues. For d>=12 the one-shell inequality persists; d<=8 full-lattice positivity is the proven literature theorem. Finite witnesses are not mistaken for universal infinite-lattice bounds.

value.rationale: This is a natural and complete finite-volume instability classification at the continuum critical inverse-square coupling: it determines the first lattice ball that can support a supercritical localized mode in every dimension. In the exceptional first failure dimension nine, the exact squared-radius 24 versus 23 boundary is a previously non-implied quantitative locality threshold, and its universal positivity certificate covers nonsymmetric modes. This sharp finite cutoff is useful for designing minimal supported counterexamples and finite-volume Schrödinger stability tests; it is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor a numerical restatement of global strictness.
